bluf: Ukraine's intensified deep-strike campaign, including successful attacks on Moscow's oil refinery and a semiconductor plant, is imposing mounting costs on Russia's war effort, but the Kremlin remains committed to maximalist territorial objectives and is escalating nuclear posturing with Belarus. Russia's failure to secure the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal with China highlights deepening economic strain, while NATO considers a July escort plan for the Strait of Hormuz that could affect European energy security.

sections.title: Ukraine Conflict Dynamics
sections.content: Ukrainian forces have gained territory and stabilized the frontline, partly due to Russia's loss of Starlink access in early February 2026 and Ukraine's effective long-range strikes. On May 17, Ukrainian drones struck the Angstrem Semiconductor Plant near Moscow and the Moscow Oil Refinery, degrading Russia's high-precision weapons production and fuel logistics. Russia responded with a massive 546-missile-and-drone barrage on May 17-18, targeting civilian and energy infrastructure, but Ukrainian air defenses downed most projectiles. Russian casualties remain high, averaging over 1,000 per day in 2026, and senior Kremlin officials reportedly view the war as a 'dead end,' yet Putin insists on seizing all of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts by year's end.

sections.title: Russian Nuclear Posturing and Belarus Integration
sections.content: Russia and Belarus completed the second stage of combined nuclear exercises on May 21, involving over 64,000 personnel, multiple ICBM launches, and deployment of nuclear munitions to Belarus. The exercises underline Russia's deepening de facto control over Belarus, including the stationing of nuclear weapons on Belarusian territory. Putin announced plans for the biennial 'Union Shield' exercises in 2027, potentially including a nuclear component for the first time. This posturing aims to distract from Russian military weaknesses and signal NATO that the conflict could escalate.

sections.title: Economic and Energy Dimensions
sections.content: President Putin's visit to China on May 20 failed to secure a deal on the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline, as Beijing continues to extract concessions from Moscow. Only minor bilateral agreements were signed, exposing the limits of Russia's pivot to Asia amid Western sanctions. Separately, NATO is considering a plan to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz starting in July if Iran's de facto blockade persists, a move that could stabilize global oil markets but risks confrontation with Tehran. Russia's occupation authorities continue efforts to integrate Ukraine's captured territories through forced transfers, cultural indoctrination, and economic incentives, further straining international humanitarian norms.

key_developments: Ukraine strikes deep inside Russia, hitting a semiconductor plant and Moscow oil refinery on May 17.
Russia launches a record 546 missiles and drones against Ukraine on May 17-18, causing civilian casualties.
Russia and Belarus complete large-scale nuclear exercises, deepening Belarus's integration into Russia's nuclear deterrent.
Putin fails to secure Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal with Xi Jinping, highlighting economic isolation.
NATO explores escort operations in the Strait of Hormuz from July amid Iran's de facto blockade.
outlook: In the near term, Russia will likely continue heavy aerial bombardments of Ukrainian critical infrastructure while Ukraine persists with deep strikes inside Russia. Diplomatic deadlock on both the Ukraine and Iran fronts is expected, with Russia's nuclear posturing potentially escalating if territorial losses mount. The failure of the Russia-China pipeline deal may further constrain Russia's fiscal position, while NATO's potential escort mission could become a flashpoint with Iran.
